title: Multiplying fractions
subtitle: Fractions · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can multiply fractions and mixed numbers, simplifying my answers.

key_vocab.definition: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Simplify at the end (or cancel first).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can multiply fractions and mixed numbers, simplifying my answers.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: multiply fractions -- To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Simplify at the end (or cancel first).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply tops together, multiply bottoms together. Cancel common factors for simpler working.
&frac{a}{b} × &frac{c}{d} = &frac{a×c}{b×d}
Straight across: top × top, bottom × bottom

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{2}{3} × &frac{4}{5} = &frac{8}{15}  (multiply across)
  ✓ &frac{3}{4} × &frac{2}{3} = &frac{1}{2}  (cancel 3s first)
  ✓ 1&frac{1}{2} × &frac{2}{3} = &frac{3}{2} × &frac{2}{3} = 1  (convert then multiply)
  ✗ &frac{2}{3} × &frac{4}{5} = &frac{6}{8}  (added instead of multiplied)
  ✗ &frac{2}{3} × &frac{4}{5} = &frac{8}{5}  (only multiplied tops)

sections.title: Worked Example
Fraction of a whole number
sections.content:
Find each fraction of the number.

(a) &frac{1}{3} × 12
(b) &frac{2}{5} × 30
(c) &frac{3}{4} × 24
(d) &frac{5}{8} × 40
